what: the objaverse index build is a node script that reads three datasets at pinned commits
why or how it was checked: a rebuild that reads main can quietly produce a different index, and a reviewed denylist would then point at a different set; the four pinned commits travel inside the index file, and the sha256 of every download is checked

what: the index ships the 20,000 best rows as public/objaverse/index.json.gz, and it is committed
why or how it was checked: 1.05 MB gzipped is what the app serves, and a rebuild reproduces the same bytes, so there is nothing to regenerate on every clone; the 840 MB of inputs stay in .cache, which is ignored

what: the build drops no fan art, nothing explicit, no figures, and nothing the app would refuse
why or how it was checked: the filters call the app's own resultPasses rule over the title and the caption, so the build and the app cannot disagree; the fan art and explicit guards come from src/safety/content.ts and the four word lists match the python prototype entry for entry; the first version of this filter used the build's own whole-word guard, which kept 491 rows the app's run scan refused, so a fish called Seabass and a Low Poly Assault Rifle were in the index but unshowable, and the app's rule was itself a run scan, which refused a Bookshelf and a Tropical palm; the rule for a title is now a whole token and nothing else

what: the licence filter keeps only the per-object CC BY 4.0 rows
why or how it was checked: the objaverse collection is ODC-By v1.0 but each object carries its own licence, and only CC BY 4.0 may be shipped and attributed; 93,281 of 789,195 rows are CC BY-NC, CC BY-NC-SA, CC BY-SA or CC0 and are dropped

what: objaverse++ is licensed ODC-By v1.0, and the hub tag of other is only a coarse bucket
why or how it was checked: the dataset card at the pinned commit ac892800fd29db09c2b560bdfdd3c57253045836 says license_name odc-by-v1.0 and license_link opendatacommons.org/licenses/by/1-0, and the TCXX readme says ODC-By v1.0; the captions and the scores are ODC-By and the objects are CC BY 4.0, so all three are credited

what: a title is cleaned by one shared function, and an empty title falls back to the caption
why or how it was checked: the sketchfab titles are raw user text, and the title is what the app shows and the matcher reads; tidyName in src/objects/objaverse-index.ts is used by both the commons path and the index, so a name reads the same from either source

what: the cap3d csv is streamed once, after the metadata filters, and not joined in memory
why or how it was checked: the csv holds 1.6 million captions, and a map of them does not fit in the heap; the metadata is filtered first and the csv is then walked keeping only the captions of the rows still alive, which peaks at about 1 GB of heap

what: the build filters: 18 steps in order, the fan art and explicit guards on known strings, the licence, age, figure and size filters, and the title cleaner, 39 tests

what: the objaverse funnel leaves 92,296 usable rows of 789,195 at score 3
why or how it was checked: a real run of scripts/objaverse-index.ts against the pinned data: 789,195 objaverse++ rows, 695,914 under CC BY 4.0, 255,342 at score 3, 207,791 after the shape filters, 155,611 after the character filter, 147,657 after the content filters, 92,296 after the size filter

what: the index is 1.05 MB gzipped at 20,000 rows and 3.15 MB at 50,000

what: two builds from the same pinned data give the same file
why or how it was checked: the sha256 of public/objaverse/index.json.gz was 83d6c74d3f9c360b9e45dc6d826415a32b10865892932f90b3ccadeef63ce596 on both runs, byte for byte

what: the caption and both exports carry the credit of a searched model, and the export header is scanned like the art
why or how it was checked: CC BY and CC BY-SA ask for the author, the licence, a link to the source and a note that the work was changed, so all four are shown; the header carries a third party title, so it goes through scanLine the same way the art does

what: the credit text is scanned but its link is not
why or how it was checked: a scan replaces one letter in place, so a scanned url would point at nothing and the licence asks for a link to the source; the words around it are scanned, and the url is left whole

what: a searched hit is skipped when its title or its description fails the content rule, and the search moves on
why or how it was checked: the typed prompt already went through checkTyped, so a searched result was the one path with no rule at all; the hit is dropped before it is downloaded, so a refused row costs nothing

what: the description is read to 300 characters, not to the 80 the caption uses
why or how it was checked: a hit can hide in the second sentence, and the title alone left the description unchecked; the extra 220 characters cost nothing because the api already sent them

what: the raw file name is checked too, not only the title
why or how it was checked: a title is cut to 80 characters, so a refused word past the cut would survive, and the credit's link is built from the raw name; the name is checked so a link that names a refused thing never reaches the caption

what: the content rule over 721 live commons hits
why or how it was checked: 29 titles and 49 descriptions were refused, all of them substring false positives: the letters of a blocked word inside an innocent word, such as ass inside class, bass and compass; the rule for a result is now a whole token and nothing else, so a Compass, a Bass Guitar and a Seabass are searchable again, and the run scan stays where it belongs, in the exported ASCII and in typed input

what: search: the description is read, a refused hit is skipped and the next one is taken, for models and for drawings
why or how it was checked: src/objects/search.test.ts, 10 tests

what: the credit and the export header: the caption shows the credit, the export carries it, and a blocked title never reaches an export
why or how it was checked: src/objects/prompt.test.ts, 11 tests in the credit and header suites

what: the smithsonian set is the one to fetch from the source, and the google scanned objects and nasa sets are skipped
why or how it was checked: each set was measured at its pinned revision rather than from its card: the smithsonian set holds 3,451 rows and 30 of 30 sampled rows parsed as one object, but 92.4 per cent of its titles are latin binomials so it does not answer a plain word without a map, and 3d-api.si.edu answers a headless user agent with a rejection page; the google set holds 1,029 glb members in 43 tar shards and 30 of 30 sampled rows rendered well, but the median glb is 7,692,276 bytes and only 569 of 1,030 fit under the 8 MB ceiling; the nasa set is skipped because its terms are a permission written around educational and informational use that says nothing about the copyright status outside the united states; the numbers and the licences are in docs/objaverse-datasets.md, and how each was measured is written up in its how to reproduce section, which gives the api calls as commands and the rest as method

what: the index keeps dropping every model that is a figure or a character, and the denylist does not reopen them
why or how it was checked: of the 207,578 rows clean on every other count the figure filter dropped 38,871 and the category filter a further 13,096, a quarter of the clean rows, against 7,773 for the franchise words; the denylist holds models rather than words, so it cannot say a statue is fine and a statue of a named character is not, which is the distinction the issue turns on; of the 20,000 rows the index ships, 1.4 per cent have a title that names a figure or a person, and most of those are false positives of the measure, such as hand gun, hand grenade and pirate ship

what: the chat box is a fifth source rather than a fifth backend in the prompt chain, and its model is reached through this app's own endpoint
why or how it was checked: a prompt that searches for a thing and a prompt that has a thing written for it are different waits and different failures, so they are different sources; the key cannot ship in a bundle, so the browser posts to /api/scene and the dev and preview servers hold the key from .env, which is ignored; a static build therefore has no chat box and says so instead of drawing a different kind of object

what: the scene writer is glm-5.3-flash on the opencode zen gateway, measured against five other models
why or how it was checked: one prompt each, sequential: glm-5.3-flash 12.9 s and a scene; deepseek-v4.1-flash 24.9 s and a scene; kimi-k2.7-code cut short at the completion cap; qwen3.8-flash over 150 s; grok-4.6 answered 400; glm-5.3 cut short before the cap was raised to 20k tokens for the reasoning trace; SCENE_MODEL overrides it

what: the model's code runs against a hand-picked namespace, behind a name check, in the worker, under an eight second deadline
why or how it was checked: the code comes from a model and a shared ?chat= link carries whatever prompt its author typed, so it is untrusted: sceneThree holds geometry and material constructors and no loader, the check refuses constructor, prototype, globalThis, self, window, document, fetch, localStorage and an endless loop before anything runs, new Function is called in strict mode so this is undefined at the top of the body, and what comes back is held to 400 parts, 120000 triangles and finite bounds; the assertions in src/objects/scene.test.ts include a FileLoader that is undefined and a prototype chain that is not a constructor

what: a scene is cached by prompt and seed in memory and in localStorage, forty entries deep, and a scene that failed is not cached
why or how it was checked: a scene costs the model ten to twenty seconds, so a repeat prompt, a reload and a share link already opened on this machine are free; the seed is the reroll, so variant asks for a different reading rather than the same one; a failure is not remembered, so trying again is one call

what: the reply is two labelled lines found independently, and a refusal buys one corrective turn
why or how it was checked: the first measured run lost three scenes to label order (one opened at CODE: with no title, one put TITLE: after the body) and one to window.innerWidth; the parser finds the title anywhere, names a scene after its prompt when the title is missing, and the endpoint re-asks once with the refusal named before giving up

what: the spike: 10 of 10 prompts produce a scene this app can run, median 11.6 s, slowest 17.2 s, 1148 to 5468 triangles
why or how it was checked: node --env-file=.env scripts/scene-spike.ts --model glm-5.3-flash --out <path>, ten prompts, each parsed, checked and run through the sandbox; the same run before the parser and retry fixes was 6 of 10

what: the app draws all ten and every one reads as its prompt at full size on the canvas
why or how it was checked: HTTrack-free CDP run on the dev server at 6000 glyphs: each prompt opened as a ?chat= link, waited on the stage's own rendering phase and held three seconds so the StrictMode double-assemble settled, then screenshotted and judged one at a time with a vision model; a contact sheet at a fifth of the size loses one of the ten, which is a size of the picture rather than of the scene

what: time to first glyph frame: 9.8 to 22.8 s for a fresh scene, 3.3 s for a repeat prompt
why or how it was checked: measured from navigation in the same CDP run on this machine (Windows 11, RTX 3090, headless Chrome); the model reported 7.2 to 20.3 s of writing; the budget is 25 s fresh and 4 s cached, and both bounds sit above the slowest measurement

what: the chat path: the sandbox, the reply parser, the cache, the share link and the endpoint contract
why or how it was checked: src/objects/scene.test.ts, src/objects/generate.test.ts, server/scene-prompt.test.ts and src/engine/url.test.ts, 33 new tests of 285 in the eighteen tracked test files; the keyless-claim test in src/objects/prompt.test.ts now holds the reverse promise, that the client carries no credential and one relative endpoint

what: the ten prompts are ten prompts
why or how it was checked: a category the set does not cover (a face, an animal in motion, two subjects in one scene) could read far worse and the measurement would not show it; one prompt in about thirty requests came back 502 twice in a row and needed a second attempt

what: the composer refuses a blocked word and keeps the object, variant asks a different question, and a static build says the box is unavailable
why or how it was checked: CDP against the dev server and against dist/ served by python -m http.server: a blocked word typed into the box showed the refusal and left the Utah teapot on screen; variant produced a second scene (1820 then 1804 triangles) with 'asking the scene writer' in between; the built files answered 'the scene writer is not available on this server' because there is no endpoint behind them, which is what makes the README's claim about a static build true

what: the scene runner executes the writer's code, and the code-scanning alert that flags it is suppressed with the mitigation named rather than hidden
why or how it was checked: this is the feature: issue 29's option C is a model writing three.js code, so the string is untrusted by construction and CodeQL is right to flag new Function at src/objects/scene.ts; four things hold it (the name check before it runs, a namespace with no loader in it, strict mode so this is not the global, and a worker with no document under an eight second deadline), and the alternative that removes the class of risk (a scene described as data rather than code) is recorded here as considered and not taken, because the measured pass rate belongs to code the model writes
